note: Second seed list, derived by a rule independent of seed set A (field-events-seed.json) so that recall can be measured on events the author did not pick. Derivation: take every Fields Medal (1936-2026) and Abel Prize (2003-2026) citation as paraphrased on the English Wikipedia pages 'Fields Medal' and 'Abel Prize' (fetched 2026-10-16); keep a citation iff the cited work combines or imports across at least two MSC two-digit sections or creates a new area; drop it if the same event is in set A; one event per kept citation (two for Talagrand). Each event records the prize record it came from. Citations were written from memory and are checked in `spotChecks` below only where noted. Laureate years for 2025 and 2026 and paraphrases are from the Wikipedia pages and were not re-checked against the IMU or Abel Committee.
mscSections: two-digit MSC sections each event is expected to link, for the channel B spike

events.name: Cobordism: homotopy theory computes manifold invariants
events.summary: Manifolds up to cobordism are classified by homotopy groups of Thom spaces, turning geometric questions into computations in stable homotopy theory.
keyWorks: R. Thom, Quelques proprietes globales des varietes differentiables, Comment. Math. Helv. 28 (1954) 17-86

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Cobordism theory

events.name: Exotic spheres: algebraic topology reaches differential structures
events.product: Differential topology of spheres; surgery theory
events.summary: Characteristic classes and homotopy groups are used to show manifolds homeomorphic to the 7-sphere can be non-diffeomorphic, then to classify homotopy spheres.
keyWorks: J. Milnor, On manifolds homeomorphic to the 7-sphere, Ann. of Math. 64 (1956) 399-405
M. A. Kervaire and J. W. Milnor, Groups of homotopy spheres: I, Ann. of Math. 77 (1963) 504-537

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Exotic differential structures on the 7-sphere

events.name: Higher algebraic K-theory
events.summary: Homotopy-theoretic constructions (plus construction, classifying spaces) define K-groups of rings in all degrees, importing topology into algebra and number theory.
keyWorks: D. Quillen, Higher algebraic K-theory I, in Algebraic K-theory I, Lecture Notes in Math. 341 (1973) 85-147

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Higher algebraic K-theory

events.name: Geometric invariant theory and moduli
events.summary: Nineteenth-century invariant theory is recast as a quotient construction for group actions on varieties, giving moduli spaces of curves and bundles.
keyWorks: D. Mumford, Geometric Invariant Theory (1965)

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Moduli varieties; algebraic surfaces

events.name: Nonlinear PDE proves the Calabi conjecture
events.summary: The complex Monge-Ampere equation is solved with a priori estimates, producing Ricci-flat Kahler metrics and showing a topological condition forces a metric.
keyWorks: S.-T. Yau, On the Ricci curvature of a compact Kahler manifold and the complex Monge-Ampere equation, I, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 31 (1978) 339-411

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Calabi conjecture; positive mass; Monge-Ampere equations

events.name: Quantum groups from statistical mechanics
events.summary: Algebraic structures behind the Yang-Baxter equation of solvable lattice models are formalised as deformations of enveloping algebras, linking to knot invariants and representation theory.
keyWorks: M. Jimbo, A q-difference analogue of U(g) and the Yang-Baxter equation, Lett. Math. Phys. 10 (1985) 63-69
V. G. Drinfeld, Quantum groups, Proc. ICM Berkeley 1986, vol. 1 (1987) 798-820

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Langlands program; quantum groups

events.name: Viscosity solutions: control theory meets PDE
events.summary: Dynamic-programming value functions, merely continuous, are given a rigorous notion of solution for fully nonlinear first and second order PDE.
keyWorks: M. G. Crandall and P.-L. Lions, Viscosity solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi equations, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 277 (1983) 1-42

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Nonlinear PDEs motivated by applications

events.name: Ramsey-theoretic dichotomies in Banach space theory
events.summary: Infinite Ramsey theory and descriptive set theory are used to prove dichotomies for Banach spaces and to construct spaces answering the unconditional basic sequence problem.
keyWorks: W. T. Gowers and B. Maurey, The unconditional basic sequence problem, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 6 (1993) 851-874
W. T. Gowers, A new dichotomy for Banach spaces, Geom. Funct. Anal. 6 (1996) 1083-1093

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Banach space geometry; Gowers' dichotomy

events.name: Deformation quantization of Poisson manifolds
events.summary: The passage from classical to quantum observables is solved for every Poisson manifold by a formality theorem using string-theory-inspired graph integrals.
keyWorks: M. Kontsevich, Deformation quantization of Poisson manifolds, Lett. Math. Phys. 66 (2003) 157-216

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Witten's intersection number conjecture; Vassiliev invariants; quantization

events.name: Sullivan's dictionary: rational maps and Kleinian groups
events.summary: Iteration of rational maps is matched term by term with the theory of Kleinian groups, so results and techniques of one side suggest and prove statements on the other.
keyWorks: D. Sullivan, Conformal dynamical systems, in Geometric Dynamics (Rio de Janeiro 1981), Lecture Notes in Math. 1007 (1983) 725-752
D. Sullivan, Quasiconformal homeomorphisms and dynamics I: Solution of the Fatou-Julia problem on wandering domains, Ann. of Math. 122 (1985) 401-418
C. T. McMullen, Complex Dynamics and Renormalization, Annals of Math. Studies 135 (1994)
secondary: Dennis Sullivan's work on dynamics, arXiv:2306.06290 (2023)

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Holomorphic dynamics; geometrization of 3-manifolds

events.name: A^1-homotopy theory and motivic cohomology
events.summary: Homotopy theory is rebuilt over schemes with the affine line as the interval, giving motivic cohomology and the proof of the Milnor conjecture.
keyWorks: F. Morel and V. Voevodsky, A^1-homotopy theory of schemes, Publ. Math. IHES 90 (1999) 45-143
V. Voevodsky, Motivic cohomology with Z/2-coefficients, Publ. Math. IHES 98 (2003) 59-104

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Motivic cohomology; Milnor conjectures

events.name: Random partitions, representation theory and Gromov-Witten theory
events.summary: Measures on partitions defined by Schur functions are analysed as determinantal point processes, and the same structures compute Gromov-Witten and Hurwitz invariants.
keyWorks: A. Okounkov, Infinite wedge and random partitions, Selecta Math. (N.S.) 7 (2001) 57-81
A. Okounkov and R. Pandharipande, Gromov-Witten theory, Hurwitz theory, and completed cycles, Ann. of Math. 163 (2006) 517-560

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Probability, representation theory, algebraic geometry

events.name: Measure rigidity and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity
events.summary: Entropy and measure-rigidity methods for diagonal group actions show that Hecke eigenfunctions on arithmetic surfaces do not concentrate, a quantum chaos statement.
keyWorks: E. Lindenstrauss, Invariant measures and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity, Ann. of Math. 163 (2006) 165-219

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Measure rigidity in ergodic theory

events.name: Landau damping: plasma physics to nonlinear PDE
events.summary: A prediction of plasma physics from 1946 is proved for the nonlinear Vlasov equation in Gevrey regularity, using analytic norms and a new treatment of echoes.
keyWorks: C. Mouhot and C. Villani, On Landau damping, Acta Math. 207 (2011) 29-201

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Landau damping; Boltzmann equation convergence

events.name: Higher composition laws and arithmetic statistics
events.summary: Gauss's composition of quadratic forms is extended to cubes and higher spaces via prehomogeneous representations, and geometry of numbers counts the resulting number fields and ranks.
keyWorks: M. Bhargava, Higher composition laws I: A new view on Gauss composition, and quadratic generalizations, Ann. of Math. 159 (2004) 217-250

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Geometry of numbers; ranks of elliptic curves

events.name: Perfectoid spaces and tilting
events.summary: Characteristic p and characteristic 0 p-adic fields are related by an equivalence of Galois groups extended to geometry, moving results from one side to the other.
keyWorks: P. Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Publ. Math. IHES 116 (2012) 245-313

prize.name: Fields Medal
prize.citationParaphrase: Arithmetic algebraic geometry over p-adic fields

events.name: Entropy of dynamical systems from information theory
events.summary: Shannon's entropy is turned into an isomorphism invariant of measure-preserving transformations, settling that Bernoulli shifts with different entropy are not isomorphic.
keyWorks: A. N. Kolmogorov, A new metric invariant of transitive dynamical systems and automorphisms of Lebesgue spaces, Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 119 (1958) 861-864
Ya. G. Sinai, On the notion of entropy of a dynamical system, Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 124 (1959) 768-771

events.name: Wavelets
events.summary: Multiresolution ideas from signal processing and quantum field theory are merged with harmonic analysis to give orthonormal bases of compactly supported functions.

events.name: Shannon capacity of graphs and the Lovasz theta function
events.summary: A coding-theory quantity for graphs is bounded by a semidefinite programme, giving the theta function and its exact polynomial-time computation for perfect graphs.
keyWorks: L. Lovasz, On the Shannon capacity of a graph, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 25 (1979) 1-7

prize.name: Fields Medal

events.name: Rational homotopy theory via differential forms
events.summary: Homotopy types are encoded by commutative differential graded algebras of polynomial forms, so rational homotopy becomes homological algebra.

prize.name: Abel Prize

events.name: Concentration of measure
events.summary: Isoperimetric inequalities in high dimension give sharp deviation bounds for Lipschitz functions, used for Banach space geometry and probability in product spaces.

prize.name: Abel Prize

events.name: Spin glasses: the Parisi formula
events.summary: A replica-symmetry-breaking prediction for the free energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model is proved by interpolation arguments and ultrametricity.

events.name: Buildings: geometry of algebraic groups

events.name: Faltings: Mordell's conjecture via moduli and heights
events.summary: Finiteness of rational points on curves of genus at least 2 is proved by combining the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties, moduli of abelian varieties and height theory.

events.summary: Ergodic-theoretic arguments on homogeneous spaces force lattices in higher rank semisimple groups to be arithmetic, tying Lie theory, ergodic theory and number theory.
